compilerSite.compiledMslAuditBasis: The exact assembled production NSString source was compiled with Xcode 27.0 build 27A266a, Metal 32023.921, macOS SDK 27.0, metal3.2, no-fast-math, warnings as errors, and the explicit SDK isysroot. AIR inspection proves one unflagged fadd for L1, one unflagged fadd for SCATTER_ADD, and the exact singleton VARIANCE sequence of two fdiv, one fsub, and one fmul with no unsafe flags, fadd, or FMA. Each kernel retains its certified source order and one static output store.

siteInventory.operation: load_word followed by uint sign-bit clear and as_type<float>
siteInventory.proof: Each ordinal is loaded exactly once. Integer sign clearing is the exact raw ABS transform for zero, subnormal, normal, infinity, and NaN classes without payload truncation.

The loop starts at ordinal one, advances by one while below N, and assigns the sole safe-mode addition result to the only accumulator. Thus N leaves induce exactly N-1 actual additions and no zero leaf or parallel partial sum.
The final L1 accumulator bits are stored once without numeric conversion, epsilon, finite substitution, or pre-truncation.

siteInventory.operation: one four-byte load_word before the update loop
siteInventory.proof: Each target thread owns one target and captures its base word exactly once. If no update ordinal matches, the same integer word reaches the sole store.

The loop starts at ordinal zero, increments by one through all U occurrences, and invokes the sole safe-mode addition only when the fully prevalidated index equals the owned target. Duplicate targets are not filtered.
One target-linear writer chooses the raw base word when unaddressed or the site-chain accumulator when addressed and reaches one static four-byte serialization loop. No atomic operation exists.

The metadata-owned raw binary32 +1 operand feeds the first explicit typed DIV relation. Its finite exact-value equation is x / 1 = x, infinity retains its source sign and class, NaN remains NaN, and the enclosing primitive site admits only DAZ/RNE/FTZ presentation.

The sole source value and immediately preceding mean feed the typed SUB exact-value relation restricted to this trace's reachable domain. It forms their exact signed difference in 2^-149 units: same-sign exact cancellation yields positive zero, while a same-sign zero/subnormal difference has magnitude below 2^23 and is exactly representable. Equal signed infinities yield NaN. No claim is made for unreachable general finite subtraction.

The typed MUL relation is restricted to the trace's same-sign zero/subnormal square. It forms the exact product numerator in 2^-298 units; the operand magnitude proof places that numerator strictly below the 2^148 halfway point, so nearest-even selects exact positive zero before the enclosing FTZ publication. No claim is made for unreachable general finite multiplication.
The square and the same metadata-owned binary32 +1 operand feed the final typed DIV relation; its explicit divisor and exact-value equation retain positive zero, while NaN class propagates.

siteInventory.operation: one as_type<uint> followed by store_word at canonical cell zero
siteInventory.proof: One dispatched thread reaches one static four-byte store. Scalar and retained [1] forms share the same canonical cell and no second writer or publication path exists.

specialValueProof.zero: Raw ABS clears either input zero sign. Every later add is represented by the exact/RNE/DAZ/FTZ site relation; raw store preserves the device-selected permitted result bits.
specialValueProof.subnormal: A raw ABS leaf remains exact. At an addition site each subnormal operand is exact or same-sign zero under DAZ, and each subnormal rounded result is exact or same-sign zero under FTZ; the Lean relation admits no third choice.
specialValueProof.normal: Every finite normal contributor enters exactly one ordinal addition, and no source branch filters, rescales, or truncates it.
specialValueProof.infinity: ABS maps either infinity sign to positive infinity. Safe binary32 addition with non-NaN nonnegative contributors retains positive-infinity class; finite overflow may also publish positive infinity.
specialValueProof.nan: ABS preserves exponent and payload fields while clearing only sign. N=1 stores those raw bits directly. For N>1, the signed NaN premise is constrained to L1-reachable operands: a NaN may carry either sign, while every non-NaN source or intermediate operand is sign-clear; safe addition then publishes NaN class without a finite fallback.
specialValueProof.daz: The formal primitive relation enumerates exact input or same-sign zero only for a subnormal input.
specialValueProof.ftz: The formal primitive relation enumerates exact rounded output or same-sign zero only for a subnormal rounded output.

varianceSpecialValueProof.zero: Both input zero signs follow the four named sites to exact positive zero.
varianceSpecialValueProof.subnormal: Every exact-or-DAZ input and exact-or-FTZ intermediate choice yields a zero or subnormal difference whose square rounds to exact positive zero.
varianceSpecialValueProof.normal: DIV(x,+1) is exact, SUB(x,x) is positive zero, and the remaining multiply and divide preserve positive zero.
varianceSpecialValueProof.infinity: Either infinity sign reaches infinity minus itself and therefore a NaN-class result through the remaining two sites.
varianceSpecialValueProof.nan: Every NaN payload/sign enters the literal site sequence and the proved result class remains NaN; no payload-specific output is promised.
varianceSpecialValueProof.daz: The formal relation admits exactly retained subnormal or same-sign zero presentation.
varianceSpecialValueProof.ftz: The formal relation admits exactly retained subnormal or same-sign zero publication.
varianceSpecialValueProof.outputForms: Rank-zero and retained [1] outputs target the same canonical scalar cell.

formalProofBoundary.proved: The Slice-1/2 L1 and SCATTER_ADD results remain intact. Singleton VARIANCE additionally defines typed DIV plus trace-domain-exact SUB and MUL primitive-result relations over signed exact values, with complete per-site DAZ/FTZ alternatives. The SUB relation covers only same-sign exact cancellation or same-sign zero/subnormal differences; the MUL relation covers only the same-sign zero/subnormal square. The exact literal DIV(x,+1), SUB(x,mean), MUL(d,d), DIV(square,+1) trace proves every finite singleton yields positive zero and either signed infinity or NaN yields NaN class, then proves the shared scalar/retained canonical cell, exactly one dispatched thread, and exactly one store.
formalProofBoundary.primitivePremise: The audited MTLMathModeSafe source and unflagged AIR instructions instantiate each typed relation on exactly the reachable Task-0069 operands; the proof intentionally makes no statement about general finite SUB/MUL outside that trace. Native preflight fixes both runtime DIV operands to the raw binary32 +1 word and restricts the custom domain to canonical FLOAT32 [1], axis [0], correction zero, no gradients, and distinct buffers. The pre-existing non-domain VARIANCE structural recipe remains direct MPSGraph rather than being diverted or rejected.
formalProofBoundary.forbiddenAssumptions: Both Lean files compile without sorry or axiom declarations. No arbitrary Word-to-Word primitive contract, asserted aggregate outcome relation, associativity, commutativity, finite fallback, payload classifier, canonical NaN, reciprocal rewrite, FMA, tolerance, retry, or deterministic exceptional-value bit pattern is assumed.
